title: speculative-decoding-and-model-integration-draft-4
content:
Summary
-------
This draft describes the speculative decoding prototype and the proposed model-integration workflow for the serving runtime. It covers: kernel implications, scheduler changes, KV cache interactions, acceptance criteria for canarying, rollback strategy, and the key telemetry/metrics we need to make safe deployment decisions. This is an engineering-first working doc — expect rough edges, TODOs, and open questions.

Background / motivation
-----------------------
Speculative decoding (SD) lets us parallelize generation by predicting likely future tokens using a cheaper model or faster execution path, validating predictions against the main model, and accepting prefixes when they match. Benefits we care about: lower p50/p95 token latency, improved throughput (tokens/s) on GPU clusters, and cost reduction via fewer autoregressive steps on the expensive path. We need a safe integration into Redwood's runtime so that:
- correctness/regressions are measurable and bounded
- fallbacks/rollbacks are quick and deterministic
- scheduler and kernel choices cooperate with KV caching and batching

Design overview
---------------
1) Two-path strategy
   - Speculative path: runs on a cheaper kernel or smaller model (quantized 4-bit variant / smaller LM) to propose k-step token prefixes. Runs with low-latency kernel and aggressive batching.
   - Verifier/main path: the canonical model that must produce identical tokens for accepted prefixes. If mismatch occurs, verifier will generate remainder starting from mismatch point (classic SD approach).

2) Kernel & execution implications
   - Speculative kernel constraints: optimized for short sequences, high throughput for small batches. Prefer fused attention kernels and int8/4 quantized matmul kernels where accuracy loss is acceptable.
   - Verifier kernel constraints: full-precision path or validated quantized variant. Must support exact probability comparisons for acceptance heuristics.
   - Kernel selection policy (proposal): extend kernel selector to be aware of SD-use-case. New input keys: "speculative_candidate" flag, preferred_latency_profile, expected_prefix_length. Selector must consider memory layout for KV cache and whether kernels preserve exact logits ordering (important for acceptance checks).

3) Scheduler changes
   - Continuous batching must be speculative-aware. Scheduler will group speculative tasks by expected prefix length and model pair (spec model + verifier) to maximize reuse.
   - Priority policy: verification tasks pinned to higher priority queues to minimize tail for rollbacks. Speculative tasks can be asynchronously batched in best-effort lanes.
   - Backpressure: if verifier lag > threshold, throttle speculative proposals for that model pair to avoid queuing large amounts of speculative state.

4) KV cache interactions
   - KV caching must be multi-versioned per-request when using SD. A lightweight speculative KV delta is stored alongside canonical KV. We avoid mutating the main KV until a speculative prefix is accepted.
   - When verifier accepts prefix, apply KV delta atomically (small write transaction) to main KV and update cache TTLs.
   - Rollback: on mismatch, discard speculative KV deltas and fallback to canonical KV state; scheduler must re-enqueue verifier generation from mismatch point using main KV.

Acceptance and metrics (canary gating)
--------------------------------------
We will gate rollout on a combination of correctness (token-match metrics) and performance gains. Minimum acceptable thresholds for initial canary:
- Target latency improvement: p50 token latency improvement >= 20% and p95 improvement >= 10%
- Match rate: accepted speculative prefixes (length >= 1) >= 92% on canary traffic; mismatch rate <= 8%
- Quality regression guardrail: end-to-end eval prompts (representative prompt set) must show no more than 0.5% ROUGE/BLEU/regression in key eval metrics vs baseline for 3 consecutive runs.
- Cost: per-token GPU compute reduction >= 10% on canary workload (after accounting for verifier compute)

Operational metrics to collect (per-request and aggregated)
- speculative_proposed_prefix_length_distribution (histogram)
- speculative_accept_rate (per-model, per-route)
- speculative_mismatch_rate_by_position (first mismatch position distribution)
- additional_verifier_tokens_generated_per_request (mean/p95)
- combined_p50/p95 token latency and verifier-only latency
- CPU/GPU utilization delta vs baseline
- tail rollback amplification: fraction of requests where mismatch caused additional >X tokens on verifier
- user-visible error/regression alerts tied to eval prompt set failures

Instrumentation details
- Tag requests that used SD with route/model metadata. Trace must include: spec_model_id, verifier_model_id, spec_prefix_length, accepted_bool, mismatch_pos, KV-delta-size, kernel_ids used.
- Emit tracing spans for: speculative-generation, verification-generation, KV-apply, KV-discard. Spans must be joinable in Console for per-request debugging.
- Logs: concise mismatch record (request id, mismatch_pos, top-5 token diffs) emitted at INFO for canary; debug logs kept behind sampling for production.

Canary and rollout plan
-----------------------
Phase 0 — lab validation (dev infra)
- Run end-to-end tests on dev cluster with synthetic load. Validate acceptance heuristics and KV delta correctness.
- Compare outputs on canonical eval set (1000 prompt set) and measure metrics above.

Phase 1 — internal canary (internal prod traffic, 1–3 engineers)
- 1% of internal traffic, 2 models (one L2 quantized small model as spec, or cheap kernel). Monitor metrics hourly.
- Gate: speculative_accept_rate >= 92% and p95 latency improvements observed.

Phase 2 — external canary (small subset of customer routes)
- 5–10% of external routes with low-risk SLAs. Add automatic rollback triggers (see next) and alerting.

Phase 3 — ramp & opt-in
- Gradual increase, run for 2 weeks, collect cost metrics. Offer opt-in for Dedicated/private customers initially as beta.

Rollback & safety controls
------------------------
Automatic rollback triggers (samples evaluated every 5 minutes):
- speculative_mismatch_rate_exceeds 12% over 10m window -> auto-disable SD for that model pair
- p95 latency regression vs baseline (increase >10%) -> auto-disable SD globally for route
- End-to-end eval failure (automated eval set) -> pause rollout and alert SRE/product

Fast manual rollback path:
- Feature flag per-customer/per-route in Control Plane. Flip causes: speculative scheduling turned off, speculative KV deltas rejected, existing speculative tasks drained.
- Safe drain period: 10s default, configurable. After drain, all new requests take canonical path.

Compatibility & edge cases
--------------------------
- Deterministic model mismatch: When models are non-deterministic (sampling), acceptance must rely on probability threshold heuristics rather than exact token equality. For initial beta we restrict to deterministic decoding (greedy/beam) or temperature=0 when using SD.
- Long prefix acceptance: limit speculative prefix length to avoid massive rollbacks. Proposal: max speculative prefix = min(8, seq_len_remaining / 2).
- Multi-turn chat: maintain speculative KV per-session. If a user updates context mid-speculation (e.g., tool call), discard speculative state and re-run canonical path.

Open questions / TODOs
- Acceptance heuristic refinement: exact-match vs probability-threshold vs top-k agreement. Need small-scale AB to determine best balance. (Jira SRV-789 assigned)
- Memory overhead estimation for speculative KV deltas across 100k concurrent sessions — profiling required.
- Kernel correctness: ensure quantized kernels used by spec path maintain monotonic logit ordering necessary for comparison heuristics. Action: run kernel unit tests that compare top-k ordering vs reference FP32.
- Cost accounting model: incorporate verifier work and added system overhead in per-token cost model.

Implementation milestones (proposed)
- M1 (2 weeks): prototype speculative path and KV-delta mechanism in dev cluster; unit tests for KV atomic apply/discard.
- M2 (3 weeks): scheduler changes for speculative-aware batching; kernel selector extension.
- M3 (2 weeks): tracing & metrics plumbing; canary harness.
- M4 (2 weeks): internal canary + iterative tuning.

References and related artifacts
- existing drafts: speculative-decoding-and-model-integration-draft.json (early ideas)
- perf benchmarks: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks#speculative
- Jira: SRV-789 (speculative-decoding epic)
- PR: serving-runtime/pull/1123 (speculative scheduling WIP)

Appendix: quick checklist before external canary
- [ ] Kernel unit tests: top-k ordering preserved across kernels
- [ ] KV delta stress test under 100k concurrent sessions
- [ ] End-to-end eval run with baseline comparisons (ROUGE/BLEU/LL) and smoke tests
- [ ] Alerting + dashboard for key SD metrics
- [ ] Feature flag controls implemented in control plane + SDK toggle

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally pragmatic: we prioritize observable safety (metrics + fast rollback) over aggressive initial optimization. Expect adjustments to acceptance thresholds after internal canary.
- Please add comments inline where you see risks or missing instrumentation.
